newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-IJAZ CENTURY STEERS PAKISTAN PAST SRI LANKA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-IJAZ CENTURY STEERS PAKISTAN PAST SRI LANKA.

text.p: Pakistan's Ijaz Ahmad completed his seventh test century after surviving a controversial run-out mix-up on the third day of the first cricket test against Sri Lanka at Colombo's R. Premadasa Stadium on Monday.
Pakistan moved to 255 for six at lunch in reply to Sri Lanka's first innnigs total of 330.
When Ijaz was on 98 he played a ball from Muthiah Muralitharan to skipper Arjuna Ranatunga at short mid-wicket and set off for a single.
Salim Malik at the non-striker's end responded initially, but suddenly turned his back on the run which left both batsmen at the non-striker's end.
First, English umpire David Shepherd gave Ijaz out. The batsman angrily made his way to the pavilion and was replaced by Inzamam-ul-Haq.
The new batsman was about to take guard when Shepherd, after advice from third umpire K.T. Francis, reversed his decision and recalled Ijaz, declaring Salim Malik out instead.
A relieved Ijaz then went on to complete a well deserved century in 276 minutes off 204 balls with 11 fours.

He received a reprieve at 109 when substitute fielder Sajeeva de Silva missed a head high catch at long-on off Kumar Dharmasena, but on 113 he became off-spinner Muralitharan's third victim of the morning.
Muralitharan had Ijaz caught at point by Dharmasena and followed it up by bowling Moin Khan two balls later for a duck.
Muralitharan also picked up his first wicket of the innings when substitute fielder Ruwan Kalpage pulled off a brilliant diving catch to his left at short mid-wicket to dismiss Inzamam-ul-Haq for 12.
Asif Mujtaba (four) and Saqlain Mushtaq (two) were the batsmen in at the break.
Scores: Sri Lanka 330 all out. Pakistan 255 for six at lunch (Ijaz Ahmed 113, Rameez Raja 50, Salim Malik 58, M. Muralitharan three for 58).
